entries.title: Citations without a note can search the web
entries.body: On an article you added, pressing Open in Sources on the card of a citation with no note asks the AI to search the web for that work's own page: where its DOI, a paper's permanent identifier, leads, or its page on the arXiv preprint archive. A one- or two-sentence note is kept only if every sentence is backed by words quoted from that page and a separate AI check agrees. It is labelled "From a web search"; if none is found, Sources says so.

entries.title: Privacy page names two more paper indexes
entries.body: The privacy page also describes Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex, two public indexes of research papers that the app can be set up to ask about the works an article cites, by a paper's identifier or by its title, for articles added from a public web address. These lookups run only if switched on; with them off, nothing is different.

entries.title: Reopening an article returns to your paragraph
entries.body: Reopening an article, or opening a link to a place in it, could land short of the right spot, and each reopen started a section further back. The paragraph you were reading is kept at the top of the screen while the page finishes loading, and your place is remembered by paragraph rather than by section.
